briefs.headline: Nearly half of festive sales of smartphones were financed
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Nearly one in two smartphones sold in India this festive season was bought on finance. As higher memory costs pushed up handset prices, brands offered shallower discounts and leaned on no-cost EMIs to ease the upfront cost. Financing accounted for 48% of festive purchases, according to estimates from Counterpoint Research.
Festive discounts narrowed to 10-25% from 35-40% a year earlier. Even after discounts, entry-level phones generally cost more than they did last year. Brands also used bank offers and trade-ins to draw shoppers, but many buyers put off upgrades. Unit sales fell 22% year on year between Oct 8 and Nov 10, almost twice the 12% drop Counterpoint had forecast. The average selling price rose 28%, keeping the market's rupee value broadly flat. Smartphone sales fell 19% year on year in the Oct 8-18 (roughly between Navratri and Dussehra) in the first wave, with online sales weaker than in earlier sale events.
"Buyers who needed a phone still bought one, often on EMI, but many others simply held on to what they had," said Shubham Singh, research analyst at Counterpoint. "Overall, smartphone sales this festive season were driven more by need than by festive sentiment," he added.
Counterpoint had projected that financing would account for 42% of smartphone sales in 2026 as a whole, up from 35% in 2025. Its earlier tracking found that non-bank lenders accounted for about two-thirds of financed handset purchases whereas the rest came through credit- and debit-card EMIs. Financing was already common at phone shops in smaller cities before the festive sales. In April-June, buyers used EMIs for 57.5% of smartphone purchases at physical stores in tier-2 cities and for more than half in tier-3 and smaller markets.

briefs.headline: Small Finance Banks reduce microfin loan portfolio after stress
briefs.bodyText:
CHENNAI: Disbursements by Small Finance Banks (SFB) for microfinance are on the decline. It is the fallout of stress in the microfinance sector over the past two years, which impacted net profit of several SFBs last year. Now, these institutions are diversifying their portfolios to de-risk the loan book.
ESAF Small Finance Bank reported a 65% YoY (Rs 4,844 crore (Q2 FY26) vs Rs 1,704 crore (Q2 FY27)) and 28% QoQ (Rs 2,366 crore Q1 FY27) decrease in its microfinance portfolio comprising group loans. Its executive director George K John said the stress experienced by the microfinance sector over the past two-and-a-half years has reinforced the need for a more calibrated, responsible and sustainable approach to lending. "We have responded by strengthening credit underwriting, enhancing collection efficiency, monitoring household indebtedness more closely and reassessing the overall composition of our loan portfolio.
"However, the reduction in our traditional group-based microfinance portfolio is not merely a response to sectoral stress. It is also part of a conscious strategic transformation of our lending model. We are progressively transitioning eligible customers who have demonstrated satisfactory repayment behaviour and have moved beyond traditional microfinance requirements into our emerging household (EHL) lending segment," he told TOI.
Shrinking advances
EHL caters to various categories of borrowers including individuals, small entrepreneurs and farming households. While unsecured lending within this segment is restricted to individual loans, other categories are predominantly secured.
Another leading SFB player, Equitas Small Finance Bank, has brought down its microfinance exposure sharply from 20% to 12% of the total advances over the past one year. Its microfinance and micro loan advances stood at Rs 6,331 crore as of Sept 30, 2026. During an interaction three weeks ago (Nov 2, 2026), its former MD & CEO P N Vasudevan said microfinance is under control this year. "Now, about 90% of our loan book is secured," he added.
Data sourced from Sa-Dhan, an association of impact finance institutions and an RBI-recognised self-regulatory organisation (SRO) for microfinance institutions (MFIs), show that the volume of loans disbursed by SFBs has reduced by 6% YoY from Rs 35,030 crore (FY25) to Rs 32,807 crore (FY26).
It stood at Rs 16,541 crore in H1 FY27. Jiji Mammen, ED & CEO, Sa-Dhan, said the share of SFBs in the total microfinance portfolio remains 15% to 16%. "The only change is that their share in securitised assets is rising in percentage terms, which is also a regulatory requirement," he said. Noting that SFBs still have the same absolute microfinance portfolio size, though their percentage share must have come down, he said, "Some of these SFBs are also actively supporting MFIs through term loans or as BC partners. So, I do not see any major challenge in this."
Mammen further said the stress experienced in the microfinance sector during FY25 and FY26 is a thing of the past.

briefs.headline: China's $1.7 trillion AI rout turns hot trade into losing bet
briefs.bodyText:
China's AI stock trade, once a hot bet as the nation's technology powerhouses raced to catch up with the US, has morphed into a losing strategy.
Stocks listed on three tech-focused indexes have shed a combined $1.7 trillion in market value since the end of June, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Multifold gains in the first half of the year that pushed the likes of upstart model developer Z.AI Co and optical module maker Zhongji Innolight Co to record highs have quickly faded.
The unravelling of the global AI boom has hit China particularly hard, as frothy valuations and reliance on policy support left stocks vulnerable once cracks emerged. The appeal of Chinese AI as an affordable alternative to pricier US models and the nation's pursuit of a self-sufficient chip chain is also being tested as the US tightens restrictions on technology exports.
The market is set for another turbulent session on Monday, after anxiety over the viability of the AI trade turned into a full-blown rout in the US. A KraneShares exchange-traded fund tracking China's Star 50 gauge fell more than 4% in US trading.
It's a painful reckoning for investors who chased China's AI rally as the 'DeepSeek moment' stunned the world.
(This is a Bloomberg story)

briefs.headline: Loans to micro firms have larger multiplier effect: RBI governor
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra has called on banks to increase lending to micro enterprises and smaller economic segments, saying that disbursing Rs 1,000 crore to a corporate benefits one business while lending the same amount to micro enterprises could benefit more than 10,000 families.
At a financial inclusion camp in Mawal taluka, Malhotra said banks needed to extend banking and credit services to people in rural areas and smaller businesses. The camp was attended by Nidhu Saxena, MD and CEO of Bank of Maharashtra, Rajneesh Karnatak, MD and CEO of Bank of India, and Sukhwinder Kaur, DMD of SBI.
Pointing out that loans to micro enterprises have a larger multiplier effect, Malhotra said financial inclusion initiatives should focus on extending banking, credit, insurance and pension services to remote areas, with greater participation of women in the formal financial system. He also stressed the need to improve digital awareness and protect customers from financial fraud. "Greater emphasis must be placed on supporting small businesses and micro-enterprises, where access to credit can improve the lives of many families," he said.
Malhotra cautioned people against investment offers promising returns of 20%, 30% or even 40% over short periods, saying these were often associated with hidden risks or fraudulent schemes.

stories.deck: With New Zealand still 146 runs behind and 39 overs remaining, the dropped chance could yet prove consequential

New Zealand continued to blunt India’s attack as the visitors found themselves needing five wickets to force a rare Test win in the country.
At tea on the fifth day of the first Test at Basin Reserve, the hosts were 206 for five, with 39 overs left to negotiate.
Having lost two wickets in the morning session, New Zealand tightened its approach further, adding just 87 runs in 51 overs in the first two sessions for the loss of three wickets. Kamboj, who had been consistently clocking the mid-130s, induced Blundell to play at a delivery outside off. Rishabh Pant, who caught the ball between his pads, did not hear the nick and was initially unsure. But captain Shubman Gill at covers and Dhruv Jurel at midwicket were convinced, prompting India to go upstairs. The replays confirmed the edge, ending Blundell’s stubborn resistance.
Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips, however, continued to prioritise survival over scoring, leaving India with little margin for error as the overs ticked away.
India had another opportunity to make inroads when Kamboj extracted extra bounce to surprise Mitchell. The New Zealand batter gloved the delivery, but Devdutt Padikkal, stationed at forward short-leg, could not hold on to an attempted left-handed catch.

stories.headline: 'Every single person knew': De Villiers backs Khawaja over Sandpapergate claims
stories.deck: De Villiers, who played in the Cape Town Test and scored 64 in the first innings and 63 in the second, has now spoken about the Sandpapergate controversy and the recent claims made by former Australia players Usman Khawaja and Cameron Bancroft.
stories.bodyText:
South African cricket great 
AB de Villiers
 has said he has no doubt that every Australian player knew about the ball-tampering during the 2018 series against South Africa, even before the infamous Cape Town Test.
De Villiers, who played in the Cape Town Test and scored 64 in the first innings and 63 in the second, has now spoken about the Sandpapergate controversy and the recent claims made by former Australia players 
Usman Khawaja
 and 
Cameron Bancroft
.
Bancroft recently revealed that sandpaper had been used during the second Test before the Australian team was caught in the third. However, De Villiers believes the Australians were also involved in ball-tampering during the opening Test in Durban.
"I'm not here to burn any individuals or say one is right and the other is wrong. I have my strong feelings about a couple of things that I might share on here," De Villiers said on his YouTube channel.
"Usman, nothing wrong with him releasing the book. The timing is obviously a bit weird given it's 2026 now."
"It's become really personal for all the people involved and I do have sympathy for them. Obviously not sympathy for what took place on that day and who knows how many games before then," the former South African captain said.
De Villiers said the claims about ball-tampering in Port Elizabeth were not the only ones, adding that he believed the same had happened in Durban.
"I see everyone is sort of admitting that in Port Elizabeth that it also happened. I can very much tell you Durban was no different. Go look at the footage. Absolutely no doubt in my mind," he said, in an explosive claim.
He also said the focus on whether players knew about the sandpaper was missing the larger issue, which was that the team had planned to break the rules.
"It's weird because everyone is now talking about the sandpaper and 'did you know about the sandpaper?'. At the end of the day, everyone knew they were going to cross the line and do something illegal and that's the point everyone is missing.
"Why are we all so worried about the object that was used? The fact of the matter is there was a pre-meditated decision made to do something illegal on the ground.
"Every single person knew about it, I have zero per cent doubt about it."
A Cricket Australia investigation had held only then-captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, who used the sandpaper, responsible for the incident.
Khawaja, who has since retired, brought the controversy back into focus in his autobiography, claiming that the entire team knew about the plan. His close friend Warner also backed his claims.
Bancroft later made a similar allegation in a newspaper column, saying "it was the whole team" and that he felt "angry and betrayed" by Test captain Pat Cummins. This came after Cummins denied knowing about the ball-tampering plan.
Former Australia Test bowler Chadd Sayers has also supported Khawaja's claims, contradicting Cummins' denial that he knew about the plan.

stories.headline: ILT20 | ‘We need to stay on the same standard as the foreigners’: UAE's Aayan Khan
stories.deck: Aayan Khan’s $95,000 move to Dubai Capitals for ILT20 Season 5 is more than an auction milestone. The UAE all-rounder discusses learning from international stars, how franchise cricket has shaped his development, and why the league’s playing conditions offer crucial opportunities for UAE and Associate players to compete, improve and earn bigger opportunities.
stories.bodyText:
Dubai:
 For 
Aayan Khan
, the value of the ILT20 is not just about sharing a dressing room with some of the biggest names in T20 cricket, but learning from them and applying those lessons to his own game.
The 21-year-old UAE all-rounder enters Season 5 with Dubai Capitals, who secured his services for $95,000 at the auction. Having spent four years in the competition with the Gulf Giants, Aayan believes the exposure to international stars has helped him improve, not just in franchise cricket but also at the international level, where he's played 48 ODIs and 40 T20Is.
“I need to do well in this league. To do well, I need to learn so many things from these international players. They have been playing franchise leagues all around the world. If I can see what they do on the field and apply that in my game, it should help me,” Aayan told TimesofIndia.com.
His move to Dubai Capitals brings another opportunity to share a dressing room with established names such as Faf du Plessis, Marcus Stoinis, Phil Salt and Noor Ahmad. Having previously played alongside the likes of Andre Russell, Sunil Narine, Kieron Pollard and Nicholas Pooran, the UAE youngster says the initial nervousness of being around international stars has gradually given way to familiarity.
“I was a bit nervous at the start, but now I know these international players. They are so good to be around. They know me, and we know each other,” he said.
Aayan Khan played four seasons with the Gulf Giants in the ILT20. (Creimas)
For the UAE and Associate players, however, the value of the ILT20 extends beyond exposure. The competition's playing conditions mandate at least two UAE players, two Afghanistan players and one ICC Associate Member player in every playing XI, creating regular opportunities for regional talent to compete alongside international stars.
Teams must also maintain a minimum of four UAE and four Afghanistan players in their squads, alongside representation from Ireland, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and another Associate nation.
Aayan sees the UAE-player requirement as an opportunity rather than added pressure, with consistent performances potentially opening doors to other franchise leagues.
“For us, two players to play in all the games is a big thing. If we do well, we get to play more franchise leagues,” he said, adding that UAE players must strive to maintain the same standards as their international teammates.
For us, two (UAE) players to play in all the games is a big thing. If we do well, we get to play more franchise leagues
Aayan Khan
“We think that we should stay on the same standard as the international players. We don't feel like, because we are from the UAE, that we are different. They make us feel that the international players and us are on the same page.”
Aayan's own journey has been rapid. He became the youngest player to feature in a men's T20 World Cup when he made his debut at 16 during the 2022 tournament in Australia. However, his career has also had setbacks, including a period away from the UAE national team, making his return a lesson in patience and resilience.
He believes Associate cricket has grown considerably in recent years, with players increasingly making their mark on international and franchise platforms. Competitions such as the ILT20, he feels, can further accelerate that progress by giving Associate players more opportunities to perform at a higher level.
Aayan Khan has played 48 ODIs and 40 T20Is for the UAE. (Creimas)
For now, his focus is on helping Dubai Capitals win. The auction price, he insists, does not bring additional pressure.
“It does not add much pressure. It is a happy moment for me. The team has shown interest in me, and I am happy to be in this new team. Hopefully, we do well this year,” he said.
Beyond the $95,000 signing, the larger opportunity is what Aayan hopes to take away from the season — more experience, a better understanding of the game and the confidence to compete with the best. For UAE cricket, the challenge is to turn such opportunities into sustained progress, with players increasingly able to translate franchise exposure into the international stage.

stories.headline: Alcaraz charges past world number one Zverev to clinch ATP Finals title
stories.deck: ‘I’ve been ‌through really difficult moments within myself, with my team, and we went through everything playing great tennis; this trophy is something I have been chasing for a really long time,’ said Carlos Alcaraz
stories.bodyText:
Seven-time Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz powered past world number one Alexander Zverev 6-2 7-6(7) on Sunday (November 22, 2026) to win his maiden ATP Finals title.
Also read | ATP finals 2026: Alcaraz has the momentum while Zverev motivated to silence critics
The Spaniard, who came back at the U.S. Open after a four-month break due to a wrist injury, saved three set points in the tiebreak before completing his 14th consecutive victory and ending the year with a third straight title, having also triumphed in Vienna and Paris.
The 23-year-old, who is the youngest man to have completed the career Grand Slam, secured the biggest tour title that had eluded him after finishing runner-up at the ATP Finals last year.
Since losing in the quarter-finals of the U.S. Open, he has won four titles with a 22-1 record.
"For me it's been an amazing week," Alcaraz said. "I couldn't have ended the week in a better way. I'm just really proud and really happy with everything I have done this week."
"I've been through really difficult moments within myself, with my team, and we went through everything playing great tennis. This trophy is something I have been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me."
For Zverev, the defeat brought an end to his most successful season, in which he won his first two Grand Slam titles and rose to the top of the world rankings.
Alcaraz initially faced little resistance from a sluggish Zverev, who had not dropped a set en route to the final. The German struggled with his usually booming serve and made 19 unforced errors in the first set.
What had been billed as a blockbuster turned out to be a one-man show after Alcaraz bagged an early break to love to take control of the first set.
Zverev, a two-time ATP Finals champion, had saved all six break points he had faced during the group stage but on Sunday he was struggling to keep pace with Alcaraz from the start.
The Spaniard earned five break points during the German's first two service games, converting one of them. By the end of the fifth game, Zverev had racked up 15 unforced errors.
While the Spaniard buzzed around the court with his trademark intensity, chasing down every ball and nodding along to the music in the arena during the changeovers, Zverev looked sluggish and slow.
He did earn one break back to cut Alcaraz's lead to 4-2 but only three points later his frustration boiled over when he argued with the umpire over a time violation warning.
The second set looked to be following a similar pattern with Alcaraz keeping the level high and earning another early break.
But Zverev won three games on the trot to lead 5-4 and eventually forced a tiebreak. He could not convert any of his three consecutive set points, however, before Alcaraz clinched the win.

briefs.headline: Tempers flare! Pakistan player gives Harshit Rana a fiery send-off, teammate steps in
briefs.deck: Harshit Rana engaged in verbal disputes with Pakistan A players during the Asia Cup Rising Stars match. This tension began during Pakistan A's innings and continued after his dismissal. Pakistan's Sufyan Moqim exchanged words with Rana as he left the field. India A ultimately lost the match by 48 runs despite strong performances by Tilak Varma and Abhishek Sharma.
briefs.bodyText:
India A pacer Harshit Rana was at the centre of a heated exchange with Pakistan A players during their Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 match at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium in Doha on Sunday. The tension continued even after Rana was dismissed, with Pakistan spinner Sufyan Moqim appearing to exchange words with the Indian pacer as he walked back to the dressing room.
Rana was dismissed for a duck in the 45th over. As he made his way off the field, Moqim appeared to say something to him. The Pakistan spinner then had to be held back by one of his teammates as tempers threatened to boil over.
Rana, Pakistan players involved in heated exchanges
The tension between the two sides had started much earlier in the match.
During Pakistan A's innings, Rana was involved in a couple of heated exchanges with the opposition's opening batters. Rana also gave Pakistan batter Shamyl Hussain a fiery send-off after taking his catch off Ayush Badoni's bowling.
With emotions running high between the arch-rivals, the exchanges continued when Rana came out to bat. His dismissal only added to the tension, with Moqim appearing to give him an aggressive send-off.
Tilak, Abhishek fight in vain as India A lose
Meanwhile, India A suffered a 48-run defeat against Pakistan A in their Group B match of the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament.
Skipper Tilak Varma's measured hundred and Abhishek Sharma's attacking 70 were the positives for India A in their chase of 314 on a challenging surface.
Abhishek kept India's hopes alive with a 42-ball knock that included six fours and six sixes. However, once he was dismissed, the other Indian batters struggled to score quickly against Pakistan's bowlers.
India A were eventually bowled out for 265.
Earlier, middle-order batter Nawaz scored a quick 79 to help Pakistan A post 313 all out. A regular member of Pakistan's senior white-ball teams, Nawaz brought up his half-century off 82 balls, hitting five fours and four sixes.
Openers Maaz Sadaqat (59 off 63 balls) and Shamyl Hussain (33 off 23 balls) also gave Pakistan a strong start. The duo added 66 runs in just 7.5 overs.

briefs.headline: Howler in the field! Gill furious as Akash Deep makes a mess of easy run-out chance
briefs.deck: The incident took place in the 74th over, shortly after lunch, when Washington Sundar was bowling.
briefs.bodyText:
India missed an opportunity to break New Zealand's fifth-wicket partnership when Akash Deep failed to collect the ball cleanly and run out 
Daryl Mitchell
 on the fifth day of the first Test in Wellington on Monday.
The incident took place in the 74th over, shortly after lunch, when 
Washington Sundar
 was bowling.Mitchell came down the track and pushed the ball towards mid-on before setting off for a single. However, Tom Blundell did not respond to the call, leaving Mitchell stranded more than halfway down the pitch. Akash Deep had enough time to collect the ball and complete the run-out but failed to gather it cleanly, allowing Mitchell to return to his crease.
"Mark that down," said former New Zealand cricketer Ian Smith on air, as India captain Shubman Gill was seen expressing his frustration at the missed opportunity.
However, Anshul Kamboj later had Blundell caught behind to break the partnership.
FOLLOW LIVE
Earlier, Washington and pacer 
Prasidh Krishna
 had taken a wicket each to keep India's hopes of a win alive. New Zealand went into lunch at 157/4, having scored just 38 runs in the first session. 
Blundell was batting on 14, while Mitchell was on eight.
Overcast conditions and the breeze from the Southern End of the Basin Reserve helped Washington generate drift, while Prasidh also improved his bowling in the second innings.
New Zealand had started the day 233 runs behind and were looking to avoid an innings defeat. Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra focused on defending their wickets and using up time on a pitch that had shown no signs of deterioration.
However, what India batter Dhruv Jurel had observed on Sunday evening came into play on the fifth morning. It was not the condition of the pitch but the overhead conditions and the breeze that helped the bowlers find some assistance.
Conway, who hit seven boundaries while largely focusing on defence, added 72 runs for the third wicket with Ravindra. The pair negotiated the opening spells of Jasprit Bumrah and Anshul Kamboj without losing a wicket.
Washington then gave India their first breakthrough of the session. Bowling into the breeze, he drew Conway forward, but the ball bounced more than the batter expected. Rishabh Pant anticipated the bat-pad chance and completed the catch while diving forward.
Prasidh, who had faced criticism for his lengths in the first innings, then dismissed Ravindra. He bowled a delivery slightly short of a length on the fourth-stump line, cramping the left-hander as he attempted a square cut. Ravindra could only manage an outside edge, which KL Rahul, positioned slightly wide of second slip, held on to.

briefs.headline: 'I could have finished game': Tilak rues Shahbaz's dismissal after Pakistan defeat
briefs.deck: Chasing 314, India A were struggling at 129/6 before Tilak and Shahbaz Ahmed added 112 runs for the seventh wicket to keep their hopes alive. However, the partnership was not enough as India A were bowled out for 265.
briefs.bodyText:
India A captain 
Tilak Varma
 said the lack of partnerships in the middle order cost his team as they suffered a 48-run defeat to Pakistan A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament on Sunday.
Chasing 314, India A were struggling at 129/6 before Tilak and Shahbaz Ahmed added 112 runs for the seventh wicket to keep their hopes alive. Shahbaz scored 56 off 41 balls, while Tilak remained unbeaten on 100 off 149 deliveries. However, the partnership was not enough as India A were bowled out for 265.
Tilak felt Shahbaz's dismissal came at a crucial stage of the chase, just when the two were planning to increase the scoring rate. He believed the all-rounder's presence for another couple of overs could have made a difference to the result.
"The way Abhishek started and the way Shahbaz gave me a partnership in between was crucial. Unfortunately, when we wanted to accelerate, Shahbaz got out. Otherwise, if he could have stayed for another two overs, I could have finished the game," Tilak said after the match.
Abhishek Sharma had provided India A with a quick start, scoring 70 off 42 balls. However, his dismissal put pressure on the middle order, which struggled to maintain the required scoring rate as Pakistan's bowlers kept taking wickets.
Tilak and Shahbaz's 112-run stand for the seventh wicket gave India A some hope, but the asking rate remained above 10 runs per over for much of the chase, leaving them with a difficult task.
Tilak acknowledged the effort of Pakistan's fast bowlers but said India A also lost the game by allowing wickets to fall in quick succession.
"The second half was slightly swinging initially, in the first 10 overs. Credit goes to those two fast bowlers who bowled very good lines and lengths. But at the same time, we lost back-to-back wickets in between. Otherwise, we could have sealed the game in the 47th or 48th over," he said.
Despite scoring a century, Tilak did not consider it one of his best batting performances, saying winning the match mattered more to him than his individual score.
"I won't say that. For me, the best is winning the game. If I don't win the game, then it's not the best for me. But I always want to take it as deep as possible. Today, I was looking for that. If any other batter could have given me support, then I could have finished the game," he said.
The India A captain also spoke about the responsibility of leading the side, saying he enjoys taking charge during difficult situations.
"If you are a captain for the team, then you should take that load and responsibility. So, yeah, I honestly love doing that. At the end of the day, God is kind and he has given those runs to me," he added.
Earlier, Hasan Nawaz top-scored for Pakistan A with 79, while Maaz Sadaqat (59) and Farhan Yousaf (56) scored half-centuries to help their team post 313 all out. Pakistan's bowlers then restricted India A to 265 to complete a 48-run victory despite Tilak's century.

briefs.headline: Carlos Alcaraz scripts history, becomes just 4th player to achieve rare feat
briefs.deck: “You’re an absolute legend of our sport and you’re only 23 years old,” Zverev said during his runner-up speech. “If you retire tomorrow, it’s OK, you can just relax.”
briefs.bodyText:
Carlos Alcaraz continued his winning run by defeating Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 (7) in the ATP Finals championship match on Sunday, adding another title to his season. The victory also kept alive questions over Zverev's inability to beat Alcaraz or Jannik Sinner during his breakout year.
Alcaraz became the fourth player to win all four Grand Slam titles during his career and also lift the trophy at the season-ending tournament featuring the world's top eight players. Andre Agassi, Roger Federer and Novak Djokovic are the other three players to have achieved the feat.
“You’re an absolute legend of our sport and you’re only 23 years old,” Zverev said during his runner-up speech. “If you retire tomorrow, it’s OK, you can just relax.”
Alcaraz overcomes injury concerns
Alcaraz has been managing a left hamstring injury and played with a black elastic band around his upper thigh, along with tape around his right knee. He has continued to win matches despite the injury, having also missed four and a half months in the middle of the year because of a right wrist injury.
The Spaniard extended his winning streak to 14 matches after winning titles in Vienna and Paris before the ATP Finals. His latest victory earned him a winner's cheque of almost $5.2 million.
“It’s been an amazing week,” Alcaraz said. “I’ve been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team. ... I’m playing great tennis. So lifting the trophy is something I’ve (been) chasing for a really long time.”
Zverev won his first two Grand Slam titles this year and reached the top of the world rankings for the first time this month. However, Alcaraz also defeated him in a five-set match in the Australian Open semifinals. That was their only other meeting this year, with the Spaniard now leading their career head-to-head record 8-6.
Sinner has beaten Zverev in their last 10 meetings, including the Wimbledon final this year. However, the Italian ended his season early because of a right knee injury.
Alcaraz breaks Zverev's serve
Zverev had not lost his serve throughout the tournament before the final, but Alcaraz put him under pressure in the opening game by earning three break points. Zverev saved all three, including one with an ace after receiving a time violation warning. However, Alcaraz broke his serve in each of his next three service games.
Alcaraz controlled the match by moving Zverev from one corner of the court to the other. He also broke the German early in the second set.
Zverev loses his cool after Alcaraz's tweener
Zverev lost his temper midway through the first set after Alcaraz used a “tweener” — a shot played between the legs — to return a lob. Zverev missed the overhead that followed and threw his racket towards the baseline.
On the next point, Zverev again took too long to serve and received a first-serve penalty. He then complained to the chair umpire.
In the second set, Alcaraz produced an acrobatic overhead while falling backwards. He then pointed a finger towards his ear, asking the crowd to cheer louder.
The match looked set to end quickly, but Zverev broke back to make it 4-4 in the second set. He then had three set points in the tiebreaker but failed to convert any of them. Alcaraz took his second match point with a backhand winner down the line.
The Spaniard celebrated by dropping onto his back on the court.
Alcaraz finished with 28 winners, more than twice Zverev's 12. He also had 25 unforced errors, compared to the German's 31.

briefs.headline: Liverpool hammer ten-man United in Pochettino debut
briefs.deck: Reduced to 10 men after eight ‌minutes, United fell two goals behind within 13 and never ‌recovered as Liverpool cruised to ‌victory ⁠through goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian ⁠Wirtz, teenager Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz
briefs.bodyText:
The scale of Mauricio Pochettino's rebuilding job was laid bare on Sunday (November 22, 2026) as Manchester United crashed to a 4-0 Premier League defeat at Liverpool, their first match under the Argentine unravelling within minutes.
Also read | Michael Carrick sacked as Manchester United manager after club’s worst start to a Premier League season
Reduced to 10 men after eight minutes, United fell two goals behind within 13 and never recovered as Liverpool cruised to victory through goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, teenager Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz.
United's nightmare start to the Pochettino era could hardly have been worse as Leny Yoro was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak, and the visitors paid the price moments later when Szoboszlai curled home the resulting free kick.
Liverpool doubled their lead three minutes later when Ngumoha beat Diogo Dalot and crossed for Wirtz, who finished with an acrobatic volley.
The Reds attacked in waves after the break and the 18-year-old Ngumoha added a third in the 66th minute, sweeping home a cross from Bradley Barcola to become the youngest player to score against United in the Premier League. Substitute Munoz added to United's misery when he fired home a ball from Wirtz.
Liverpool climbed to fourth on 21 points, seven behind leaders Arsenal, while beleaguered United are 19th with just eight points and one victory to show from 11 games.

briefs.headline: Conquering the SENA summit in KLassic style
briefs.deck: Rahul isn’t given to grand, loud, garish, outlandish gestures — perhaps there is a finishing school in Bengaluru where they teach the players how to refrain from the gaudy — but then again, he doesn’t need those when he speaks so loudly, eloquently, fluently and without a pause with his bat
briefs.bodyText:
Many summers ago during an intense conversation on the art of batting in Test cricket, Sadagopan Ramesh revealed that he had received a piece of advice that blew his mind away. The left-hander from Chennai was a free-flowing opener, easy on the eye, who made batting look ridiculously simple. But as he was finding his feet in the five-day game internationally, he knew that he needed to tighten his technique simply because of the step-up in the quality of bowling that would confront him.
By the time Ramesh broke into the Test team in January 1999, in Chennai against Pakistan, Rahul Dravid had already established himself as a solid No. 3. Dravid batted at No. 7 in his first two Test innings, at Lord’s and in Nottingham, in June-July 1996, when he produced excellent knocks of 95 and 84 respectively. Within six months, in the Caribbean in January 1997, he was pitchforked to the No. 3 position, which he made almost exclusively his own until his final Test, in Adelaide 15 years later.
Chalk and cheese
Dravid’s approach to batting was as unlike Ramesh’s as chalk is to cheese. Where Ramesh thought little of playing an expansive cover-drive off the first ball of a match if he believed it was there to be hit, Dravid was a lot more conservative. That didn’t mean that Ramesh didn’t put a price on his wicket, or that guarding his wicket was Dravid’s foremost objective. Each skinned the cat his own way, which is exactly what makes the world an interesting place.
Ramesh and Dravid shared a terrific rapport, undoubtedly helped by the time Dravid spent early in career playing for India Cements. One of the most fascinating pearls of wisdom he received from Dravid, Ramesh revealed, was to learn to enjoy leaving the ball. ‘A good leave,’ Dravid told Ramesh, ‘can be as satisfying as playing the perfect cover drive’.

briefs.headline: World chess championship: Gukesh to open title defence with black
briefs.deck: The first game of the best-of-14 match against Sindarov will be played on Tuesday
briefs.bodyText:
D. Gukesh will play with black pieces in the opening game of the World chess championship match against Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva. The colours were drawn at the opening ceremony on Sunday.
The first game in the best-of-14 match will be played on Tuesday. Gukesh sounded confident going into the defence of his title, in spite of his inferior form. His rival, on the other hand, has had an exceptional year.
“Compared to the last time, it feels like I am more experienced coming into the match, but whatever has happened till now just gets erased when we sit at the table for Game 1,” the defending champion from Chennai said. “It’s a completely different match, a completely different opponent and a different place. So I am not really thinking about other things; I just want to give my best for these 14 games.”
Gukesh admitted it would be a tough test for him against Sindarov. “He has just been very consistent and in very good form,” he said. “He is surely one of the very top players who is at the very top of his game. So for sure it is going to be a real test. But I have prepared in the best way I could. I am very enthusiastic about this match, to test myself against such a strong player and to see myself what I am capable of.”
Sindarov also said it would be very hard. “But I am very happy that I have got this opportunity to play for the Word championship,” he said. “There are many chess players who play all their life but do not get this chance. After winning the Candidates in Cyprus, I have been thinking about this match for the last six months, but I have been playing and a lot of travelling in that period. I will try to enjoy the match”.
